region.text: 'All of Attica and Boeotia passed peacefully into the hands of the Catalans'

ledger.note: 1311: the Catalan Company wins at Halmyros and takes the Duchy of Athens. 'fought on 15 March 1311' at Halmyros, 'a decisive victory for the mercenaries' with Walter V of Brienne falling; 'Subsequently the Catalans took over the leaderless Duchy of Athens' and 'All of Attica and Boeotia passed peacefully into the hands of the Catalans'. The Company itself dates from 1302-1303 ('arrived at Constantinople in January 1303'; Catalan Company page, infobox 1302-1390) but becomes a territorial state only now. Livadeia surrendered at once and Athens was surrendered by Walter's widow Joanna of Chatillon; Thebes was plundered.

1312: the Company recognises the suzerainty of the Aragonese crown of Sicily. 'In 1312, they accepted the overlordship of the Aragonese crown of Sicily and adopted a new seal' (Catalan Company page); 'the Catalans recognized the suzerainty of King Frederick III of Sicily, who appointed his son Manfred as duke' (Duchy of Athens page). The state continues, now a vassal duchy of Sicily; the Kingdom of Sicily / Crown of Aragon dossiers should carry the matching vassal_start with this slug as counterpart.

region.text: Neopatras and the places taken by 1325: Zetounion, Loidoriki, Siderokastron, Vitrinitsa

ledger.note: 1319: Alfonso Fadrique's Catalans begin the conquest of the Thessalian south. 'When the Greek ruler of Thessaly, John II Doukas, died in 1318 without an heir, his domains fell into chaos'; 'Led by Alfonso Fadrique, the Catalans took Neopatras in 1319, and by 1325 had also conquered Zetounion, Loidoriki, Siderokastron and Vitrinitsa.' The Catalan Company page says the Company took 'the region of Thessaly' already in 1311; the Thessaly page dates the Almogavar occupation of the south to 1319 (after occupying forts in the south in 1310), and the Neopatras page is followed for the duchy.

ledger.note: 1319: the Catalans take Neopatras. 'Led by Alfonso Fadrique, the Catalans took Neopatras in 1319'; the duchy 'was established in 1319' with Neopatras as its capital, ruled by a vicar-general (Alfonso Fadrique 1319 to about 1330) for the infant Duke Manfred.

region.text: Zetounion, Loidoriki, Siderokastron and Vitrinitsa (the growth of the 1326 shape over the 1314 shape)

ledger.note: 1325: Zetounion, Loidoriki, Siderokastron and Vitrinitsa are Catalan. 'by 1325 had also conquered Zetounion, Loidoriki, Siderokastron and Vitrinitsa'. The page gives 'by 1325' rather than a year for each; Cliopatria's shape grows from 8,242 to 10,175 km2 in 1326. The page does not name the former owners of Loidoriki and Vitrinitsa (John II Doukas's domains are the nearest named); the page adds that the Catalans 'apparently briefly' held Domokos, Gardiki and Pharsalus.
1325: the Catalan conquest of southern Thessaly is complete ('by 1325'); the five-captaincy Duchy of Neopatras stands.

region.text: 'most of the Duchy's possessions in Thessaly'; Neopatras itself stayed Catalan

ledger.note: 1348: the Serbs conquer Thessaly and the Catalans lose their Thessalian possessions. 'Most of the Duchy's possessions in Thessaly were lost when the region was conquered by the Serbs'; 'Neopatras stayed in Catalan hands.' The Thessaly page: 'Thessaly was invaded and occupied by the Serbian Empire of Stefan Dusan' in 1348. Cliopatria's Serbian Empire row begins only in 1352 and its Catalan shapes do not change in 1348.

1377: Peter IV of Aragon takes the ducal title. 'In 1377, the title of Duke of Athens and Neopatras was assumed by Peter IV of Aragon.' The land stays under the Catalan vicars-general until 1388-1390 (Catalan Company page: 'until 1388-1390').

wars.name: Battle of Halmyros and the Catalan takeover of the Duchy of Athens

zones.text: Attica and Boeotia, which passed to the Catalans after the battle

wars.outcome: Decisive Catalan victory on 15 March 1311; Walter V of Brienne and almost the whole knighthood fell; Attica, Boeotia, Livadeia and Athens passed to the Catalans, Argos and Nauplia stayed with the Brienne loyalists.
wars.note: The battle was fought at Halmyros in southern Thessaly; some older scholars placed it near Orchomenos on the Boeotian Cephissus. No contest period is ledgered: the duchy's land was surrendered peacefully after the battle.

wars.name: Catalan conquest of southern Thessaly
wars.outcome: The Catalans under Alfonso Fadrique take Neopatras in 1319 and the places named above by 1325 and organise the Duchy of Neopatras in five captaincies.
wars.note: The Thessaly page: 'In 1319 the Almogavars occupied southern Thessaly' and formed the Duchy of Neopatria.

wars.name: Serbian conquest of Thessaly
wars.outcome: Stefan Dusan's Serbs conquer Thessaly; the Catalans lose most of their Thessalian possessions and keep Neopatras.
wars.note: The Byzantines had held Thessaly since 1332 (Thessaly page); only the Catalan side is dossiered here.

notes: Written 2026-10-19 by eu-05-e from four pages (budget up to 5). Dates and extent: start is 15 March 1311 (Halmyros); Cliopatria's Catalan row starts 1314 and the Duchy of Athens row runs to 1313, so 1311-1313 is a new keyframe copying the Duchy of Athens shape (the duchy-of-athens dossier ends March 1311 and names this slug as successor). End is 1390, not Cliopatria's 1362: the Catalan Company page says both duchies were Catalan 'until 1388-1390'; Cliopatria draws the same Greek bbox 1363-1394 inside its Crown of Aragon row, so the Crown of Aragon dossier should subtract the Greek duchies for 1363-1390 and carry them as this state's overlordship (vassal_start 1312, counterpart catalan-company). Disagreements between pages: the Catalan Company page says the Company took 'the city of Thebes and the region of Thessaly' in 1311 and converted Thessaly into the Duchy of Neopatras; the Neopatras page dates the Neopatras conquest to 1319-1325; the Duchy of Athens page says 1318/19; the Halmyros page says the Catalans had already conquered 'much of the region' of Thessaly in 1309-1311 for Walter. The Neopatras dates are followed. The Duchy of Athens page gives the Navarrese conquest of Thebes as 1379, the Neopatras page speaks of 1380; 1379 is used. Not settled: (1) who took the territory the Catalans lost between 1379 and 1380 beyond Thebes; (2) when the County of Salona ended (kept to 1390); (3) where the Company's seat was 1311-1378 (Thebes is the inherited capital, not a page's statement); (4) the 1344 and 1352 Cliopatria areas change by 24 and 123 km2 with no event on the pages; (5) the Catalan Company infobox gives no area, so no area comparison was possible. Radii: Neopatras 25 km, Athens 30 km, Salona 20 km are readings, not page statements. Gazetteer lacks the places Neopatras (Ypati), Salona (Amfissa; 'Salona' resolves to Croatia), Zetounion, Loidoriki, Siderokastron and Vitrinitsa; coordinates are used instead. Counterparts: 'Navarrese Company' (1379) is a free company that held Thebes and then Achaean lands; it has no Cliopatria row and may need a dossier. Nerio I Acciaioli's duchy of Athens (1388-1458) has no Cliopatria row and is given to duchy-of-athens.
